2609.16890.title: Cascade: Hierarchical Recoverability Control for Large Language Model Unlearning
2609.16890.paper_summary: Large Language Model (LLM) unlearning is essential for removing sensitive or copyrighted knowledge while preserving general utility. Existing methods often leave residual knowledge in intermediate representations, which can still be recovered. To address this, we propose Cascade, a hierarchical recoverability control framework that minimizes the internal identifiability of target knowledge. Cascade combines three complementary controls: path-level routing to suppress privacy-associated activation routes, representation-level compression to reduce geometric separability, and decoding-level intervention to limit residual recovery. Experiments on TOFU, MUSE-News, and WMDP, including robustness tests with query reformulation and extraction-style prompts, show that Cascade effectively reduces recoverability while maintaining stable model utility.
2609.16890.paper_summary_zh: 大型語言模型（LLM）去學習對於移除敏感或受版權保護的知識同時保持一般效用是至關重要的。現有的方法經常在中間表示中留下殘餘知識，這些知識仍然可以被恢復。為了解決這個問題，我們提出了Cascade，一個層級可恢復性控制框架，旨在最小化目標知識的內部可識別性。Cascade結合了三種互補的控制措施：路徑級路由以抑制與隱私相關的激活路徑、表示級壓縮以減少幾何可分性，以及解碼級干預以限制殘餘恢復。在TOFU、MUSE-News和WMDP上的實驗，包括使用查詢重構和提取風格提示的穩健性測試，顯示Cascade有效地減少了可恢復性，同時保持穩定的模型效用。
